summary: Ages 5-6 (Y1): recall number bonds within 20 as fact families, so each addition fact (8+5=13) hands over its related subtractions (13−5=8, 13−8=5) rather than being memorised separately. Facts should appear in all four forms and with the unknown in any position (7=16−9) to pre-empt the 'answer-after-equals' habit. Within-20 recall is built from bonds-to-10 plus making-ten (bridging) and doubles, then firmed with short, frequent interleaved retrieval, while a reconstructing strategy stays available for slips.
misconceptions: Learning additions and subtractions as separate lists rather than as fact families, doubling the memory load and leaving subtraction weak.
Recalling only the canonical form (8+5) and struggling with 5+8 or 13−8.
Rejecting missing-number/reordered forms (7 = 16 − 9) because = is read as 'answer here'.
Counting rather than recalling, especially for bridging facts.
Confusing bonds of different totals when facts aren't tied to a clear whole.

activities.title: Fact-family machine: one relationship, four facts
steps: Set a whole of 13 with two parts, 8 and 5, in a part-whole triangle (whole at the top, parts in the lower corners).
Read the four facts that the relationship generates: 8+5=13, 5+8=13, 13−8=5, 13−5=8. Say each one aloud.

Change a part (e.g. make the parts 7 and 6 with whole 13) and watch all four equations rewrite, so you see the same structure holds for every bond (for a double such as 6+6=12, the four forms reduce to two different facts: 6+6=12 and 12−6=6).

Use a 'cover a corner' mode: hide one number and say the missing one. Then set a new, clearly labelled whole (e.g. whole 16 with parts 7 and 9) and practise missing-number forms such as 7 = 16 − ? and 16 − ? = 9.
Practise shaky family members again in short interleaved rounds until the four facts come quickly from recall or near-instant derivation.
activities.insight: One relationship among three numbers IS four facts: learning 8+5 gives you 13−5 and 13−8 for free, so subtraction is derived from addition rather than memorised as a separate list.

activities.title: Build within-20 recall from bonds-to-10, making-ten and doubles
steps: Re-secure bonds to 10 first (e.g. 6+4, 7+3) so they are instant.
For a crossing-ten sum like 8+5, split the second number to make ten: 8+2=10, then 10+3=13. Use one full ten-frame and one partial frame to show the move.
Use a known double to help a near-double: 6+7 is 6+6+1 or 7+7−1.
State which facts you just KNEW and which you had to work out, then practise the worked-out ones more.
Repeat in short, frequent, mixed sessions rather than one long drill.
activities.insight: Teen bonds are not fresh rote facts: they can be derived from secure bonds to 10 using making-ten and doubles, and derivation becomes faster recall with spaced practice.

activities.title: Mixed-form retrieval practice across the fact family
steps: Answer quick-fire items drawn from all four forms of a family: 8+5=?, 5+8=?, 13−5=?, 13−8=?.
Answer missing-number items with the unknown in different positions: 7 = 16 − ?, 8 + ? = 13, ? − 5 = 8.
Mix additions and their related subtractions back-to-back (8+5 then 13−5) to practise pulling the subtraction from the addition.
Note any item that needed counting and return to it after a making-ten reminder.
activities.insight: Recognising and completing a bond in any form — including the unknown in any position — is the mark of flexible, secure fact-family knowledge.

checkQuestion: Quick-fire, try not to count on your fingers: what is 8 + 5? … Now 13 − 5? … 6 + 7? … 14 − 6?
checkAnswer: 13, 8, 13, 8 — answered rapidly from recall or near-instant derivation (e.g. make-ten), with each subtraction pulled from its related addition fact.
